assumptions: The family renewable-energy business may provide introductions or a pilot setting, but it does not provide guaranteed feedstock, customer commitments, or permission to use its resources.
Credentialed partners, rather than the venture, perform testing, legal classification, packaging, ADR transport, waste possession, and treatment.

Waste batteries continue through the statutory free producer or producer-responsibility take-back route; revenue is earned only from optional decision evidence, contracted programme administration, or completed lawful non-waste transactions.
The founder initially retains full-time employment and operates within the stated time and capital limits.
The proposed prices, transaction volumes, margins, buyer acceptance rates, insurance terms, and first-notice contract acceptance are hypotheses rather than established facts.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The revised insight is coherent: value would come from controlling notice of retirement events and assembling defensible product-versus-waste evidence, not from reselling passport data. That addresses a real coordination gap among owners, testers, buyers, carriers, and recyclers. It is not yet clear that the gap is commercially large because incumbents already orchestrate much of the same workflow.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Classification, residual-value uncertainty, safe handoff, and documentary liability create consequential pain. However, statutory free take-back gives owners an adequate zero-price fallback for waste batteries, so payment depends on the service reliably recovering incremental non-waste value or reducing material portfolio costs. No source verifies that owners, installers, producers, or buyers will pay the proposed fees.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Avoiding inventory, transport, and waste possession can limit capital intensity, and a success fee aligns payment with realized value. The economics nevertheless depend on a currently unknown share of batteries retaining positive value after testing, documentation, packaging, logistics, buyer discount, insurance, and failed-sale costs. The stated founder-wealth scenario requires 2,500 annual dispositions at 2,500 PLN blended net revenue without evidence that either volume or net revenue is attainable, while sparse events make fixed coordination and acquisition costs especially damaging.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Poland has an expanding installed storage base and a plausible installer-led commercial segment, but the reviewed figures describe recent installations rather than near-term retirements. The beachhead is still broad across battery types, triggers, chemistries, and routes, and there is no verified three-year count of reachable, economically recoverable units.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A Polish-language, installer-embedded entrant could be locally responsive, but Cling and Circunomics already offer assessment, condition analysis, documentation, trading, and logistics orchestration across Europe. The candidate has no committed exclusive supply, unique buyer access, proprietary technical capability, or demonstrated performance advantage that would support a particularly strong segment position.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Winning a standardized commercial-battery niche could extend into more installers, fleet or lease returns, EV and industrial batteries, additional disposition services, and nearby EU markets. The same compliance, chemistry, buyer-liquidity, and local-partner requirements recur in each adjacency, so expansion is plausible but not automatically cheap or fast.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Exclusive first-notice and first-inspection rights plus accumulated routing outcomes could become a compounding advantage. Those rights are currently only proposed, may require guarantees or revenue sharing, and can be contested by installers, producers, recyclers, and incumbent exchanges. Passport access is purpose-limited and non-exclusive, while counterparties can bypass a broker after a match unless contracts and continuing service value prevent it.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The offer could improve convenience and auditability relative to an owner coordinating every specialist independently. There is no evidence of a material improvement in recovery value, decision accuracy, speed, price, risk transfer, or buyer reach versus the named incumbents or established producer and recycler channels. The proposed local access advantage remains hypothetical.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: EU passport and end-of-life documentation rules, regulatory enforcement, and Poland's growing storage fleet create an emerging need to formalize battery disposition. Timing is mixed rather than clearly favorable: passports cover only newly placed batteries from February 2027, detailed access rules remain unsettled, much of the installed base is young, and falling new-battery prices pressure second-life value.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Installer maintenance and repowering relationships offer a credible route to event-level access without consumer brand building, and the founder has a relevant warm channel for learning. Yet five pilots are only a proposed test, first-notice clauses have no verified acceptance, and installers may demand guarantees or economics the venture cannot initially support. Repeatable acquisition cannot be assumed while event frequency and payer identity remain unresolved.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data skills, renewable-sector proximity, AI leverage, and no-inventory design fit a part-time pilot. Commercial operation still requires dependable battery-testing, waste-law, ADR, insurance, chain-of-custody, and buyer expertise that AI cannot substitute for. Misclassification or transport failure can create liability far beyond transaction revenue, and the proposed 10-16 weekly hours may be strained by exception-heavy partner coordination.

main_structural_strength: Contracted first-notice and first-inspection rights could create forward feedstock visibility and permissioned outcome data without requiring the venture to own, store, or transport hazardous inventory.
primary_score_limiter: The venture has not established a sufficiently frequent and profitable paid event: waste disposal has a free statutory route, while positive-value non-waste sales may be sparse and costly to prove.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The IEA evidence that second-life reuse remains constrained by safety, warranty, uncertain remaining life, repurposing cost, liability transfer, and falling new-battery prices directly threatens the depth and margin of the revised lawful non-waste transaction pool.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A binding pilot dataset should show reachable retirement-event frequency, first-notice contract acceptance, chemistry-specific testing and compliance cost, non-waste qualification and sale rate, buyer-paid price, time to close, failed-case cost, insurance terms, and contribution margin relative to free EPR take-back; it should also benchmark realized outcomes against Cling, Circunomics, and direct recycler routes.
highest_value_structural_change: Narrow the initial product to one standardized fleet or battery class and sell installers, lessors, or producers an exclusive portfolio-level residual-value recovery service with minimum annual event volume, a recurring administration fee, pass-through specialist costs, precommitted qualified buyers, and a success share; keep all waste routes free and partner-operated.
